mcq.passage: Even the most marvelous computer eventually winds up in the trash. The United Nations estimates that 20 million to 50 million tons of e-waste are created worldwide every year. 12 all those circuit-boards and plastic casings do not just vanish on their own. A lot ends up in a place called Guiyu, once a quiet fishing village on China’s coast, 150 miles from Hong Kong. Now as many as 100,000 workers do the dirty and very dangerous work of 13 and recycling the scraps, which contain toxins such as lead, mercury, cadmium, and polychlorinated biphenyls, or PCBs. A health survey done last year by nearby Shantou University found that of 165 children under the age of 6 examined in Guiyu, 82% had 14 of lead poisoning. A vast majority of the e-waste comes from the US and countries in Europe—despite rules established at the 1989 Basel Convention that banned the trading of toxic materials. China passed its own law banning the 15 of e-waste in 2002, after a report drew attention to Guiyu. But the law is ineffectual Similar operations have been found by environmental groups in Karachi, Pakistan, and Chittagong, Bangladesh.

mcq.q: Swallowing angry words is much easier than having to eat them.
opts: Holding our temper is much easier than having to apologize for our angry words.
Taking back our angry words is much easier than having to apologize for them.
Once we lose our temper, we will end up apologizing for our angry words.
Before we lash out our angry words, we had better think about the consequences.

mcq.q: In detective stories, a lot of clues are superfluous and designed to mislead the reader.
opts: In detective stories, the clues often flow by too fast for the reader to catch.
The clues in detective stories are only written to trick the readers.
There are often unnecessary clues added in detective stories to confuse or deceive the reader.
The clues in detective stories mislead the reader because they are superficial.

opts: Twain’s novel Pudd’nhead Wilson was challenged by the strong racial belief of the conservatives in his time.

Twain disputed the racial belief of his contemporary liberals in the novel Pudd’nhead Wilson.
